items.corrected_text: The city council decided on 21 March 2024 to amend the parking fee ordinance, in force from 1 September 2024: zones Ost, West and Thomasbrücke EUR 0.40 per 10 minutes (minimum EUR 0.40); zone Süd and Horexstraße EUR 1.00 per 30 minutes and EUR 1.50 per 60 minutes (minimum EUR 1.00); fees at the Parkplatz Am Heuchelbach were dropped. The amendment is signed by Oberbürgermeister Alexander W. Hetjes (28 August 2024).

'Verlagerung des ruhenden Verkehrs in die Parkhaeuser', Neuordnung Dorotheenstrasse/Loewengasse, Verbesserung des Verkehrsflusses auf dem Umgehungsring; OB Hetjes named; main goals reduce emissions and ensure accessibility; wording is 'soll'/planned. Report opened (stamped ENTWURF 09.10.2023, so draft). Upper Louisenstrasse (Haingasse to Rathaus) pedestrian zone crossed by roads, no Umweltzone, Luftreinhalteplan 2002, NO2 no longer at risk after Euro VI buses and an electric bus, Kaiser-Friedrich-Promenade traffic calming in the measure list: all supported. But the Altstadt zone is described as open in the daytime only to 'Anlieger' (frontage/access traffic), not 'residents'. Very weak parking relevance; air quality and Umweltzone details add little.
items.corrected_text: The mobility concept report (draft dated 9 October 2023) says the upper Louisenstraße (Haingasse to Rathaus) is a pedestrian zone, though crossed by some motor-vehicle streets, and the Altstadt parking zone is a traffic-calmed area open in the daytime only to Anlieger (access traffic). It states there is no Umweltzone in Bad Homburg, that Hesse's air quality plan for the Rhine-Main area dates from 2002, and that the NO2 limits for spa towns are currently no longer at risk after the city bus fleet switched to Euro VI and an electric bus was bought. Its measures include traffic calming of Kaiser-Friedrich-Promenade (a proposed measure).

items.note: Report opened (ENTWURF 09.10.2023). 1,868 on-street spaces in four zones, ten public garages with 2,849 spaces, about a third permit holders, 43 percent average garage occupancy (from 2018 draft concept, 2016 counts), Kurhausgarage 55 percent daytime, on-street average 64 percent with maxima of 96 percent, no serious capacity shortages: all in the report. Problems: the 'peaks above 90 percent in 2019' figure is from the Kur- und Kongress GmbH's own unpublished 2019 counts (footnote 36), not the 2018 concept; and the report adds that the tariff imbalance was countered in the meantime so garages are now cheaper than streets. Data are old (2016/2019). Overlaps with item 9 (same paragraph of the report).
items.corrected_text: The mobility report (draft dated 9 October 2023) describes the baseline: four managed on-street parking zones (Altstadt, West, Ost, Süd) with 1,868 spaces, and ten public garages with 2,849 spaces; roughly a third of garage spaces are used by permit holders. It cites the 2018 draft parking management concept (based on 2016 counts) for average garage occupancy of 43 percent and on-street occupancy averaging 64 percent with maxima of 96 percent; the Kurhausgarage had the highest average (55 percent in daytime hours, 07-19), reaching above 90 percent at peaks in 2019 according to the Kur- und Kongress GmbH's own counts. The report concludes there are no serious capacity shortages and attributes the garage underuse partly to street tariffs having been cheaper than garage tariffs at the time, which it says has since been corrected.

items.note: Report opened (ENTWURF 09.10.2023). Three of ten public garages privately run (Louisen-Arkaden, Horex-Parkhaus, La Vie Shopping), rest by Kur und Kongress GmbH; guidance system linked to website and Bad Homburg app; mobil-parken/smartparking mobile parking: all as stated. It is a 2023 draft statement; the city's 2026 pages list Parkhaus am Gueterbahnhof (Horexstrasse) among the Kur- und Kongress GmbH garages, so 'Horex-Parkhaus' may be a different facility. Low value; overlaps with items 8 and 10.

Page opened; title matches. '10 Parkhaeuser und 3 Parkdecks bzw. -plaetze', Parkleitsystem, 'Kur- und Kongress-GmbH betreibt aktuell 7 Parkhaeuser und 1 Parkplatz', app overview: all supported. But the 7-name live list on the page (Casino, Karstadt, Kurhaus, La Vie, Louisen Arkaden, Rathaus, Schlossgarage) is the page's map of garages with free-space counters, not the company's list of operated garages; the tariff overview shows the company's seven as Kurhaus, Schloss, Rathaus, Casino, Bahnhof, Gueterbahnhof, Karstadt. The draft wording implies the company runs La Vie and Louisen-Arkaden. Overlaps with items 9 and 11.
items.corrected_text: The city's parking page states that visitors to the centre and Kurpark can choose between 10 garages and 3 parking decks or lots, with a parking guidance system showing currently free spaces. The Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH (department Parken + Sicherheit) operates 7 garages and 1 car park. The page's garage map, which shows free spaces per garage, listed seven garages (Casino-Parkhaus, Karstadt-Parkhaus, Kurhausgarage, Parkhaus La Vie, Parkhaus Louisen Arkaden, Rathausgarage and Schloßgarage), and the Bad Homburg app gives a free-space overview per garage.

items.corrected_text: From 1 January 2023 the garage previously known as 'Parkhaus am Bahnhof' in Horexstraße was renamed 'Parkhaus am Güterbahnhof' (city notice of 9 January 2023).

items.note: Dauerparkplaetze page opened; title matches. Supported: EUR 50/month 'Pendler-Ticket' at Gueterbahnhof, regular EUR 90, night parkers EUR 45, Kurhaus and Rathaus waiting lists/no new permits due to high demand, permits offered at Schloss, Karstadt, Bahnhof, Casino, Gueterbahnhof. NOT on this page: 'limited quota' and the job-ticket/annual-pass/RMV-ticket proof (those are on the tariff overview page) and the mobility-report sentence about P+R at Gonzenheim/Ober-Eschbach (report from 2023; Gonzenheim U-Bahn station has since been closed for U2 works). The EUR 50 permit is therefore supported but the draft cites the wrong page for the quota detail.
items.corrected_text: The Dauerparkplätze page lists a EUR 50 per month Pendler-Ticket (park-and-ride) permit at the Parkhaus am Güterbahnhof (Horexstraße 1A); regular permits there cost EUR 90 per month and night parkers EUR 45. Permanent permits for the Kurhausgarage and Rathausgarage are not currently being newly issued because of high demand (waiting lists), while permits are offered for the Schloßgarage, Karstadt-Parkhaus, Parkhaus am Bahnhof, Casino-Parkhaus and Parkhaus am Güterbahnhof.

items.corrected_text: The city's 'Zukunft Kurhaus' project page features an address by Oberbürgermeister Hetjes on the planned new Kurhaus with casino operation (Spielbankbetrieb) and states that the citizens' assembly (Bürgerversammlung) took place on 19 October 2023, with a presentation of designs.

items.note: hessenschau article opened; published 09.12.25; title matches. Spatenstich on Tuesday, about 1.6 km with 355 m tunnel, about EUR 200 million with city share almost EUR 52 million 'nach ersten Prognosen', 'spaetestens 2029' closing of the gap (planned commissioning 2028/2029), 2018 Buergerentscheid over 70 percent: supported. But the article (written 9 Dec 2025) only says the U2 'faehrt am 11. Januar das letzte Mal nach Gonzenheim' (future, year not stated, 'im neuen Jahr'); the draft states as a past fact that service ended on 11 January 2026. Neither this article nor the umleitung-u2 page confirms that it happened. Target 2029 is correctly worded as targeted.
items.corrected_text: hessenschau reported on 9 December 2025 that construction had started (Spatenstich) on the extension of the U2 from Gonzenheim to Bad Homburg station: about 1.6 km with 355 m in a tunnel, costing about EUR 200 million (initial forecasts put the city's share at almost EUR 52 million), with service targeted for 2029 at the latest. The article said the U2 would run to Gonzenheim for the last time on 11 January (2026), after which buses would replace it between Ober-Eschbach and Gonzenheim, and notes that over 70 percent voted for the extension in a 2018 citizen referendum.

items.corrected_text: On 5 December 2025 the IHK Frankfurt am Main welcomed the groundbreaking for the U2 extension, scheduled for 9 December, saying the direct station connection would improve the accessibility of the Bad Homburg centre and strengthen commuter links between Bad Homburg and Frankfurt; it also notes that the Regionaltangente West is under construction.

corrected_summary: Bad Homburg's city-centre garages are run mainly by the municipal Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH, which raised garage tariffs on 1 April 2023 and moved four city-centre garages to a half-hour tariff on 1 May 2024; on-street fees and paid hours were changed in 2023 and again from 1 September 2024. The council adopted the mobility concept 2035 on 21 March 2024, whose starter measures include moving parked cars from streets into garages; the draft report's baseline (from a 2018 parking concept based on 2016 counts) found average garage occupancy of only about 43 percent. The U2 extension to the station is under construction with service targeted for 2029, the Galeria store was reported at risk in July 2026 (no closure decision), and a September 2026 tender (not yet awarded) covers new digital garage payment and access systems. The Güterbahnhof garage offers a EUR 50 monthly park-and-ride permit.
